751.title: Cartesian-Based Control Systems and Examples
751.notes: Title verifies Lecture Number25; no substantive model.

752.title: Learning Outcome
752.notes: Objectives for Cartesian schemes and implementation.

753.title: Contents
753.notes: Joint-based comparison, intuitive Cartesian control, decoupling and adaptation.

754.title: Cartesian Based Control: Comparison
754.notes: Joint errors versus workspace straight lines and task-space trajectories.

755.title: Joint-based control with Cartesian-path input
755.notes: Desired X, Xdot, Xddot enter Trajectory Conversion; joint references head toward a compressed summing circle delta theta; actual theta negatively fed back. Literal sum would mix units. Prose explicitly says IK converts Xd to theta_d; no branch choice sentence here.

756.title: Joint-Based Control with Cartesian Input
756.notes: IK, inverse-J velocity and derivative-of-inverse acceleration expression. Dot over J^-1 potentially ambiguous but correct only as total derivative of inverse; desired-branch evaluation must be explicit. Noise/delay/computation caveats. No branch-selection prose.

757.title: Direct Cartesian-Space Control
757.notes: deltaX=Xd-X, X=Kin(theta) with actual theta feedback converted before Cartesian error; coordinate-conversion-and-gains produces torque. No orientation subtraction asserted.

758.title: Advantages and Challenges
758.notes: Natural workspace specification and easier line tracking; coordinate conversion, Jacobian/inverse transforms and higher computation within loop. Benefits not unconditional.

759.title: Intuitive schemes
759.notes: Inverse-J and transpose-J controllers reduce Cartesian error through torques; overview only.

760.title: Inverse-Jacobian Cartesian Controller
760.notes: deltaTheta=J^-1 deltaX, gains produce torque; actual theta feeds forward kinematics in feedback. Formula is local displacement, assumes square invertible J if ordinary inverse.

761.title: Transpose-Jacobian Cartesian Controller
761.notes: deltaX=Xd-X; F=K deltaX; tau=J^T F. Gain-to-force-to-transpose-Jacobian diagram. Formula supports a compatible force/Jacobian frame and dimensional derivation, but those conditions are not explicitly stated.

762.title: Cartesian Decoupling
762.notes: Goal: uniform configuration-independent Cartesian tracking, critically damped fixed closed-loop characteristics and decoupled axes.

763.title: Cartesian Dynamic Model
763.notes: F=M_x(Theta) chi_ddot+V_x(Theta,Theta_dot)+G_x(Theta); force/moment, inertia, velocity and gravity terms. Base O uses uppercase X/Y/Z; point P uses lowercase x/y/z. Dashed sphere is schematic, not quantitative geometry.

764.title: Cartesian Model-Based Control
764.notes: F=M_x Fprime+V_x+G_x, with Fprime a servo-law component. Virtual end-effector force is converted to joint torque; no physical end-effector force actuator is assumed.

765.title: Cartesian Control Law
765.notes: tau=J^T F; Fprime=chi_d_ddot+K_v E_dot+K_p E. Actual theta through Kin gives position; actual theta_dot through J gives velocity. Model compensation precedes transpose-Jacobian conversion.

766.title: Cartesian Controller Structure
766.notes: Repeated control diagram lists error formation, model computation, transpose-Jacobian mapping, plant and forward kinematics. Coordinate conversions are inside feedback.

767.title: Dual-Rate Cartesian Control
767.notes: Fast servo law, slower model/background calculations. Configuration-dependent terms justified as relatively slowly varying; this is conditional, not universally true. Diagram adds G and B_x+C_x terms.

768.title: Advantages and Drawbacks
768.notes: Potential tracking/disturbance-rejection benefits versus increased computation, transforms and implementation burden. No unconditional performance theorem.

769.title: Adaptive Control
769.notes: Payload, wear, aging, center of mass, friction and inertia can change. E and E_dot plus actual joint states feed adaptation laws that update dynamic-model block. Normalized tauprime precedes model and physical tau follows it. No adaptation equation.

770.title: Adaptive Control Features
770.notes: Online model estimation and updating aim to reduce servo errors and improve dynamics compensation. No stated stability or parameter-convergence theorem.

771.title: Summary
771.notes: Recaps joint/Cartesian comparison, intuitive schemes, Cartesian decoupling and adaptive control; no extra derivation.
